Title: Tous les synodes nationaux des Eglises reformees de France, auxquels on a joint des mandemens roiaux et plusieurs lettres politiques sur ces matieres synodales. Tome premier: the Discipline as drawn up at the first national synod of Paris (May 1559; the Confession of Faith is referred to there, not printed) and the acts of the national synods from Paris 1559 to Privas 1612, with Aymon's preface and the letters of the papal nuncio Santa Croce in Italian and French
Creator: Eglises reformees de France, Synode national (the acts); Jean Aymon (1661-1735, editor, per the host catalogue; the title page names him and the privilege at file line 681 says he ceded it to the bookseller Delo); the nuncio's letters are given in Italian with a French rendering facing
Publisher: La Haye (The Hague): chez Charles Delo, sur le Cingel, a l'Esperance (imprint read in the OCR at file line 90)
Publication Date: 1710 (title page read in the OCR at file line 91 as 'M. DCC. X.'; host catalogue 1710)
Rights: Public Domain (an early eighteenth-century print; public domain by date under the project's 95-year rule)
Language: fra
Source: Internet Archive item touslessynodesna01gl, file touslessynodesna01gl_djvu.txt (Princeton Theological Seminary Library copy; collections Princeton, americana, universityofottawa, toronto), fetched directly (curl, raw bytes) by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session, second-pass agent for the continental Reformed and Scandinavian worlds), 2026-10-23; host rights statement: none on the item (no possible-copyright-status field and no licence field; not access-restricted); rights rest on the 1710 title-page date read in the OCR.
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged (no characters altered; the raw file contains 0 long-s glyphs, so no long-s normalisation was done). Rights basis restated: an early eighteenth-century print; public domain by date under the project's 95-year rule.
Content note: Tome 1 of 2; Tome 2 (the synods from Tonneins 1614 to Loudun 1659 and the later royal acts) is not vendored. This is the French text behind John Quick's Synodicon in Gallia Reformata (London 1692, vendored as quick_synodicon-in-gallia-reformata_1692.txt), which Quick made from the manuscript acts; Aymon printed the French in 1710 from the same archive, so the two are independent witnesses to one record and this file is the French beside Quick's English. Contents as the OCR shows them: the title page and the editor's address and PREFACE (from file line 193), then LETTRES ... du NONCE DU PAPE PIE IV (from line 701: Prospero Santa Croce's despatches from the French court on the Reformed churches, Italian with French facing, as the title's 'lettres politiques'), then the synods, each headed 'Synode national tenu a ...' with the acts in numbered articles: Paris, 25 May 1559 under Henri II (line 28459; the first synod, whose section opens with the Discipline in numbered articles under MATIERES GENERALES at line 28470; the Confession of Faith is referred to at lines 28546-28570 but its text is not printed in this tome), Poitiers, 10 March 1560 (29129), Orleans, 25 April (the OCR heading reads '1561 apres Paques', the second year of Charles IX; 29666), Lyon, 10 August (OCR '1565', the third year of Charles IX; 30149), Paris, 25 December (31605), Vertueil (32311), La Rochelle, 2 April (33692), Nimes, 6 May (34488), Sainte-Foy (35253), Figeac (35910), La Rochelle, 28 June (36365), Vitre (36867), Montauban (37867), Saumur (39061), Montpellier (40154), Gergeau (41358), Gap (42626), La Rochelle, 1 March (46403), Saint-Maixent (49540) and Privas (51973); the TABLE of all the synods at line 25643 lists both tomes with their years and pages (the OCR of its year column is partly garbled, so a build takes the year from each synod's own heading or from Quick); a LETTRE DE REMERCIMENT AU ROI (line 49315) and LETTRES D'AMNISTIE (line 52530) are among the royal and political pieces. Running heads give the synod number and place with the page number. OCR sampled at 10/30/50/70/90 percent (about 0.70 of tokens read as words against a clean modern-French baseline of 0.92, the Italian of the nuncio's letters lowering the 10 and 30 percent samples): the 1710 typography's long s is read as f throughout ('obeiffance', 'fufdites', 'defirant'), accents and ligatures are often misread, and the running heads and page numbers are noisy. No U+017F characters were present. SECOND WITNESS for exact wording (INTAKE scan-quality rule): locate an article here and verify against the page image, or against Quick's English, before quoting. The English of the whole is Quick's Synodicon (1692), vendored.
